summary: Asked, for the first time, whether mypintusan's six declared alarms can actually fire (tools/fleetbench/bench_pintusan_alarms.py, 19 checks; item 2 of the hardening register for the app that physically opens doors). services/controller.go declares duress, tamper, reader-offline, secure-channel, door-forced and door-held-open, each with a severity, an operator headline written to be read at 3am and a translation in four languages - and THREE OF THE SIX COULD NOT FIRE ON ANY INSTALLATION. One omission on the wire explains all three: an OSDP PD answers POLL with an ACK, or with a queued card read or keypad entry, and NEVER volunteers a status change, so LSTAT (tamper, mains) and ISTAT (the door-position contact) have to be scheduled by the CP - and infra/access/osdp's poll loop sent neither, ever. Everything downstream of that hole was built and unit-tested: the door state machine, Controller.ContactChanged, the forced and held-open events, the audit reasons, the CRITICAL severity on door-forced, and a TestBusTamperSurfaces that passed for the life of the driver by handing the bus an LSTAT itself. Measured live against a real appliance and tools/osdp-sim: opening a reader's enclosure raised nothing, a door opening with no grant and no exit request raised nothing, and a door wedged open past its threshold raised nothing - the last being the commonest way a secure door stops being one. A FOURTH DEFECT sat in the other half of an alarm: Reader.TamperState was written once as 'ok' when the reader was enrolled and never again, and Reader.LastSeenAt was never written at all, so while the reader-offline alarm fired correctly the readers screen still reported tamperState 'ok', lastSeenAt 0 - the alarm woke somebody and the screen they opened lied to them. FIXED by giving the poll loop a supervision schedule (osdp.Options.StatusInterval, default 1s, statusMillis per bus in config and runtime settings) that alternates LSTAT and ISTAT, skips ISTAT entirely on a reader whose PDCAP claims no supervised inputs (asking a keypad-only reader for a door contact earns a NAK every second, and a NAK is a failed transaction, which is what declares a healthy reader offline), and emits both on the EDGE so a reader whose case is left open reports once rather than once a second forever; by a new osdp.EventInput carrying the ISTATR contact states, which Controller.contactReported maps to the door bound to that reader and feeds to ContactChanged (input 0 is the door contact and true means open - a convention the driver now documents, since OSDP reports an input's electrical state and leaves the meaning to the installer); and by Controller.markReader + SQLStore.MarkReader persisting supervision state onto the reader row, with LastSeenAt deliberately NOT stamped when a reader is declared offline because it was last seen when it last answered, not when we gave up on it. A DEFECT THIS WORK INTRODUCED AND THE EXISTING SUITE CAUGHT, recorded because the reason is a real production failure: gating supervision only on elapsed time starved card delivery, because a card is queued at the PD and handed over on a POLL and every dead reader on a segment costs a full reply timeout - so a degraded bus can take longer to go round than the status interval, at which point every single transaction is a status command and NO BADGE IS EVER DELIVERED while the bus looks up and supervision looks healthy. Supervision is now capped at one slot in four per reader (minPollsPerStatus) as well as by time, pinned by TestBusStatusNeverStarvesCardDelivery. DoorMachine.ContactBound now answers from both sources - a myiotsan contact is CONFIGURED, a contact on the reader's supervised input is DISCOVERED - because answering only from configuration told an operator they had no forced-door detection on every door whose contact is wired the ordinary way. The simulator needed two new scenarios (contact-open, contact-cycle: the PD had always modelled Inputs and nothing had ever driven them), and tamper/silent gained card loops for the same reason refuse-sc/no-sc/wrong-key did in the previous item - a reader that never came up produces no grants and no alarms, which reads exactly like a reader that came up and whose alarm is dead. The bench's most important episode is the negative one, that a granted entry must NOT raise a forced alarm, and it is only meaningful because the door's held-open threshold is set below how long the contact stays open: door-held-open firing is the positive evidence that the opening reached the state machine, and only then is the forced alarm's absence a statement about the shunt. Seven new tests (TestBusPollsStatusUnasked, TestBusReportsDoorContactUnasked, TestBusStatusIsEdgeTriggered, TestBusStatusNeverStarvesCardDelivery, TestReaderContactRaisesForcedAlarm, TestReaderContactAfterGrantDoesNotAlarm, TestReaderTamperMarksTheReaderRow). PROVEN GOOD AND UNCHANGED: duress fires at CRITICAL (re-run as the control for the whole notification path, so that 'no alarm arrived' elsewhere is never confusable with 'the feed is broken'), and reader-offline fires at WARNING rather than CRITICAL, which is the deliberate choice alarm.go argues for. STILL NOT BUILT, REPORTED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER: the myiotsan door-contact binding (Door.ContactDeviceKey) has no path in, so a site whose contacts terminate on a relay board rather than on the reader still has no forced or held-open detection; and Controller.RequestToExit has no caller, so a REX button wired to the reader does not shunt the forced alarm. 19/19 checks pass with the fixes; 9/19 against the unfixed app (the simulator changes are bench tooling and were held constant across both runs).
compatibility: Backward-compatible; no schema change and no API change. New optional config field buses[].statusMillis (default 1000) on both config.json and the runtime access settings; omitting it keeps the default, and an existing config needs no edit. BEHAVIOURAL CHANGES AN OPERATOR WILL NOTICE, all of them alarms that were silent before: a reader whose tamper switch trips now raises an access.tamper notification and its row's tamperState changes from 'ok' to 'tamper'; a reader declared offline now shows tamperState 'offline' instead of 'ok'; Reader.LastSeenAt is now populated where it was always 0; and a door whose contact is wired to the reader's supervised input now raises access.door-forced (CRITICAL) and access.door-held-open (WARNING) where it previously raised nothing. A site that had wired a door contact to the reader and grown used to the silence will start receiving real alarms - that is the point, but it is a visible change in notification volume on installs with propped doors. Note also that the door contact's polarity is assumed, not configurable: input 0 asserted means DOOR OPEN, so a normally-closed contact wired the other way round will report the inverse and alarm continuously; per-input polarity is a reader-profile setting that does not exist yet, and a site seeing constant forced alarms after upgrading should check the wiring first. On the bus itself, an online reader now spends up to one transaction in four on supervision instead of polling; badge-to-strike latency is unaffected because queued operator commands still jump the round-robin, and the one-in-four cap exists precisely so that a degraded segment cannot let supervision starve card delivery. Scope is `infra` rather than `mypintusan`: mypintusan has no entry in infra/versioning/version.json's apps map yet, and an unknown scope token hard-fails the release run.
